description:
This package contains the code and the numerical data behind the paper

"Net electron spin rotation in a plane-wave pulse:
 Holonomy set by the anomalous magnetic moment"
N. S. Akintsov, A. P. Nevecheria, S. N. Andreev, Qing-Hua Qin,
submitted to Physical Review D.

The paper shows that the net rotation of the spin of an electron crossing a plane-wave pulse of finite duration is a holonomy. After the exact g = 2 evolution is factored out, the spin obeys a Larmor precession in the rest-frame magnetic field of the wave with the factor g/2 replaced by the anomaly a_e = (g-2)/2. The net rotation depends only on the closed curve traced by the transverse vector potential, and at leading order it is a rotation about the propagation direction through -(1/2) a_e^2 A, where A is twice the signed area enclosed by that curve. It vanishes identically at g = 2 for every polarization, and for linear polarization at every g. It does not depend on the electron energy, the carrier frequency or the rate at which the curve is traced; the pulse length, the envelope shape and a chirp enter only through the curve, and at leading order only through A. Finite focusing restores a g-independent rotation at second order in the diffraction parameter eps = 1/(k w0). In classical radiation reaction of the Landau-Lifshitz form the energy-loss term leaves the anomalous holonomy unchanged; the Schott term adds a g-independent rotation, negligible at the parameters considered.

CONTENTS

spin_magnitude.py     Plane-wave calculations: the g = 2 null test, the area
                      law, scaling with energy and pulse parameters, the
                      integrator-tolerance scan, and the longitudinal spin
                      projection and axis tilt.
holonomy_scan.py      Scan over pulse shapes, chirps, ellipticities and
                      polarization gating behind Fig. 2, the flat-top
                      resummation of its inset, and the angle-wrapping case.
focused_beam.py       Lax-Louisell-McKnight focused-beam fields, Maxwell
                      residuals, and the eps^2 violation of the area law
                      (Fig. 3).
indep_check*.py       A second, independent implementation used for
                      cross-checks.
rr_ikt_check.py       Landau-Lifshitz radiation reaction with Fermi-Walker
                      spin transport at inflated tau0, and the first-order
                      integral of a field-dressed anomaly.
make_fig1.py          Fig. 1, the curve traced by the vector potential and its
                      signed area, computed from the pulse formulas.
make_fig2.py,         Figs. 2, 3, S1, S2 from the JSON results.
make_fig3.py,
make_figS1.py,
make_figS2.py
plotstyle.py          APS figure conventions; audit() fails before a file is
                      written if any lettering or line falls below the APS
                      minimum.
reproduce_all.py      Single entry point; regenerates every number and every
                      figure quoted in the paper, and checks the deposit.
*.json, *.log         The results themselves. Every number quoted in the paper
                      and in its Supplemental Material comes from these files.
figproofs/            PNG proofs of the five figures.
legacy/               Superseded scripts from an earlier stage of the project,
                      kept for provenance. No result in the paper depends on
                      them.

REPRODUCTION

pip install -r requirements.txt
python reproduce_all.py           # full run, about 22 min on one core
python reproduce_all.py --quick   # reduced grids, about 7 min
python reproduce_all.py --verify  # check the tree against MANIFEST.sha256

Python 3.13 with NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib and SymPy; pinned versions in requirements.txt. No GPU is required.

INTEGRITY

MANIFEST.sha256 lists checksums for all deposited files. Left out are the trees this package generates (__pycache__/, quickrun/) and the trees that belong to the person running it rather than to the deposit: a virtual environment, an IDE project directory, a version-control database. The checksums are taken over raw bytes; .gitattributes stops git from converting line endings, so this archive and any clone of the repository hold exactly the deposited bytes.

SCOPE

The package reproduces the figures, tables and quoted numbers of the paper. Radiation reaction is integrated only as a classical check at inflated tau0, for a plane wave; quantum recoil is not simulated. The package does not use exact nonparaxial fields and performs no averaging over the focal volume or over beam parameters. Sections VII and VIII of the paper state what each of these omissions leaves open.

CHANGES IN v1.1.0

New Fig. 1 (make_fig1.py); figure scripts renumbered to follow the revised article (former make_fig1.py -> make_fig2.py, former make_fig2.py -> make_fig3.py); Fig. 2 relabeled and given a lower panel with the relative departure from the area law; Fig. 3 redrawn relative to the plane-wave signal; new rr_ikt_check.py (radiation reaction and dressed anomaly); documentation updated. No result file of v1.0.1 changed. New .gitattributes: the archives of v1.0.0 and v1.0.1, built from the repository, hold LF line endings where MANIFEST.sha256 expects CRLF, so their --verify fails although their content is identical; from v1.1.0 the check passes on the archive and on a clone. Details in CHANGELOG.md.
